description: Default prioritisation (MCA) matrix for the PCN v1 template: four weighted criteria scored on a shared 1–5 ordinal scale, rolling up to a weighted total, a percent-of-maximum score, and a priority band.

scale.label: Very low
scale.meaning: The project performs very poorly against this criterion. Strong argument against selection; normally requires the proposal to be reworked before it can be prioritised.

scale.label: Low
scale.meaning: The project performs weakly against this criterion. Contributes little; would need compensating strength elsewhere to be selected.

scale.label: Moderate
scale.meaning: The project performs acceptably against this criterion. Meets the minimum expectation without standing out.

scale.label: High
scale.meaning: The project performs well against this criterion. A clear, evidenced strength that supports selection.

scale.label: Very high
scale.meaning: The project performs exceptionally against this criterion. A decisive strength, fully documented and verifiable.

criteria.label: Urgency and criticality
criteria.description: How soon the intervention must happen, and what happens if it does not. Considers safety and public-health risk, remaining useful life of the asset, service gaps, and binding legal or contractual deadlines.

descriptors.1: Fully deferrable beyond 5 years with no material consequence. No service gap, no asset at risk, no legal or contractual obligation attached.
descriptors.2: Deferrable by 3–5 years. Addresses a convenience or efficiency improvement; existing assets and services remain functional in the meantime.
descriptors.3: Needed within 2–3 years. Service quality is measurably degrading or the asset is approaching the end of its useful life; risk remains manageable in the interim.
descriptors.4: Needed within 12–24 months. Significant service shortfall, accelerating asset deterioration, or a regulatory / contractual deadline that will be breached without action.
descriptors.5: Immediate action required (under 12 months). Risk to life, safety, public health or the continuity of an essential service; asset failure imminent, or a legal obligation already in default.

criteria.label: Expected economic and development impact
criteria.description: The scale and breadth of socio-economic benefit and the strength of the link to national development objectives. Where an appraisal exists, anchor the score on EIRR / ENPV against the hurdle rate stated in the submission's appraisal evidence.

descriptors.1: Benefits confined to a very small group. No measurable contribution to national or sector objectives; EIRR below the hurdle rate or ENPV negative.
descriptors.2: Localised benefits, few beneficiaries. Weak or unquantified link to development plan targets; EIRR at or marginally below the hurdle rate.
descriptors.3: Moderate benefits for a district or regional population. Supports at least one national development plan objective; EIRR at or modestly above the hurdle rate.
descriptors.4: Substantial benefits across several districts or sectors. Directly supports a priority development plan objective; strong EIRR / ENPV with measurable gains in jobs, productivity or access.
descriptors.5: Transformational, nationwide or multi-sector benefits. Flagship of the national strategy; very strong EIRR / ENPV with wide, well-evidenced returns (jobs, trade, inclusion, regional integration).

criteria.label: Environmental impact
criteria.description: Net environmental and climate effect after mitigation, plus the credibility of the mitigation plan. Note the direction of the scale: a HIGH score means a favourable environmental outcome, not a large impact.

descriptors.1: Major, irreversible adverse impacts (full EIA category). Significant resettlement or loss of protected habitat, and no credible mitigation plan in place.
descriptors.2: Significant adverse impacts requiring a full EIA and costly mitigation. Material residual impacts remain after mitigation.
descriptors.3: Moderate, site-specific impacts, manageable through a standard ESMP. Net environmental effect broadly neutral once mitigation is applied.
descriptors.4: Minor, short-term construction-phase impacts only, fully mitigated. Some positive co-benefits such as lower emissions or improved energy efficiency.
descriptors.5: Clear net-positive environmental outcome: climate adaptation or mitigation, pollution reduction, ecosystem restoration. Explicitly aligned with national climate commitments.

criteria.label: Fiscal affordability and sustainability
criteria.description: Whether the capital cost can be financed and the recurrent cost carried over the asset's life. Considers MTEF coverage, secured financing, O&M funding, and contingent liabilities.

descriptors.1: No identified financing. Capital cost exceeds available fiscal space; O&M cost unfunded and unaffordable; would breach debt or deficit ceilings.
descriptors.2: Financing uncertain and not reflected in the MTEF. O&M funding not secured; material fiscal risk from FX exposure, guarantees or contingent liabilities.
descriptors.3: Financing plausible and partly reflected in the MTEF. O&M cost identified and broadly affordable within the sector ceiling.
descriptors.4: Financing secured or formally committed (budget, IFI, verified donor or PPP). O&M fully costed and provided for in the sector budget; contingent liabilities limited and disclosed.
descriptors.5: Fully financed on concessional, grant or self-financing terms. Generates own revenue or verified savings; no additional pressure on the recurrent budget; no contingent liabilities.
